clue.text: Display concern for the entertainments industry

parts.note: to display something is to show it
a concern is a firm or business

explanation.surface: A company that puts on exhibitions belongs to the world of entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Show business is the collective name for theatre, film, television and other entertainment trades.

clue.text: She will shortly receive bill for varnish

parts.note: she will, shortened, is the contraction she'll, written without the apostrophe
AC is short for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: A woman will soon get the invoice for a pot of wood finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin dissolved in alcohol and used as a glossy wood finish.

clue.text: Goes for new spot

indicators.note: new tells us the word spot is made over into a fresh arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone picks a fresh location.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt for something is to choose it, so goes for means chooses.

clue.text: This bird flags

definitions.meaning: a small finch-like songbird of the Old World
festive strings of little flags or the cloth used for them

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a songbird family and decorative strips of flags hung at celebrations.

clue.text: Endless row coming up over people in the county

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue coming up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards
endless means the last letter of the word for row is cut off

parts.note: a row is a fuss or commotion
folk are people

explanation.surface: A never-ending quarrel arises among the inhabitants of a shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts FUSS to FUS, and 'coming up' turns it to SUF. SUFFOLK is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is one of the English counties, on the East Anglian coast.

clue.text: Name a line never in dialect

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Identify a verse that is never heard in local speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Nary is a dialect or folksy form of never, as in nary a word.

clue.text: Means to climb a wall for opera-house party

parts.note: La Scala is the famous opera house in Milan
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A climbing technique is used to get into a celebration at the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Scalado, like escalade, is the old military practice of scaling fortress walls with ladders.

clue.text: Southern bay caving in? It would make a film full of excitement and adventure

definitions.text: It would make a film full of excitement and adventure

parts.note: The Wash is a large bay on the east coast of England
buckling means giving way or collapsing

explanation.surface: A southern bay collapsing would make a dramatic adventure movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is the square bay between Lincolnshire and Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Swashbuckling describes daring adventure with sword fights, the stuff of pirate films.

clue.text: Trickery increased 100% over London borough

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: increasing by a hundred per cent means doubling
Ealing is a borough of west London

explanation.surface: Fraud has doubled across a part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-dealing is deceitful duplicity, saying one thing and doing another.

clue.text: Wholemeal, when about to have lunch, possibly?

indicators.note: about means the word for when surrounds the other piece

parts.note: having lunch is one example of eating

explanation.surface: A question about bread: wholemeal, when you are about to eat lunch?
explanation.definitionFit: Wheaten bread is made from whole wheat flour, so it is wholemeal.

clue.text: Hotch-potch of distant paper-round

parts.note: far means distant
a rag is slang for a cheap newspaper
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A jumble comes from a faraway newspaper delivery route.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or jumble, just as a hotch-potch is.

clue.text: Footpad alone?

definitions.meaning: read as foot pad, the underside of the foot

explanation.definitionFit: The underside of the foot and the adjective meaning only both share one spelling.

clue.text: Bit of a fair way, we hear, knocked up by driver

definitions.text: Bit of a fair way, we hear, knocked up by driver

parts.words: Bit of a fair way, we hear, knocked up by driver
parts.note: fair way sounds like fairway, the mown grass of a golf hole; a golfer's driver can gouge a chunk of turf from it

explanation.surface: A motorist kicks up a piece of road some distance away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' looks like a motorist but is the golf club, and 'fair way' is said like 'fairway'.
explanation.definitionFit: A divot is the piece of turf torn up by a golf club during a stroke.

clue.text: Pub bore opens with insult

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: opens points to the letter that starts the word bore

explanation.surface: A tedious drinker at the local starts with a jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting or hurtful remark, a jibe.

clue.text: Brook or a lake short of water?

parts.note: a river or tank that is low is short of water

explanation.surface: Is a stream or lake running dry?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brook' looks like a stream but is the verb, to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or permit it, usually in the negative.

clue.text: He in any trouble, laughing?

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of he and any are thrown into disorder
in trouble suggests the letters of he and any are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man in a fix still manages to laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the spotted or laughing hyena, famous for its cackling call.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is commonly called the laughing animal for its giggling cry.

clue.text: Support record arrears of work

parts.note: to back is to support
a log is a record, as of a voyage

explanation.surface: Someone backs a record of overdue tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of jobs still waiting to be done.

clue.text: Kind of surgery for the eye (privately?)

definitions.meaning: minimally invasive surgery done through a tiny incision
the small opening in a lock that a snoop peers through

explanation.definitionFit: Small-incision operations take this name, and so does the lock opening a nosy person peeps through.

clue.text: Finished with Jersey, say? Push the boat out!

definitions.meaning: a discarded garment such as a jersey, no longer wanted
the instruction to untie a boat and set off

explanation.definitionFit: A discarded piece of clothing and the sailor's order to cast loose share one phrase.

clue.text: Cat plague?

definitions.meaning: the cat o' nine tails, a whip

explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip, like the cat o' nine tails, and figuratively any great affliction.

clue.text: Wantonly sins for a thrill

indicators.note: wantonly, recklessly and without restraint, suggests letters scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Sinning recklessly for the excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a sudden shiver of excitement.

clue.text: Party to decline dressing?

parts.note: a band is a party or group of people
to age is to grow old and decline

explanation.surface: A political group refuses to get dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material used as a wound dressing.

clue.text: Cubist, perhaps, swallows one cookie

indicators.note: swallows means the rearranged letters take in the other piece
perhaps signals the letters of the word Cubist could be arranged differently

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A modern painter eats a cookie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' turns CUBIST into BISCUT, and 'swallows' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Biscuit is the British word for what Americans call a cookie.

clue.text: He loves most air-conditioning

indicators.note: conditioning means the letters of most air are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A man who most adores air-conditioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air-conditioning' reads as one word, but 'conditioning' is the anagram signal on MOST AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amorist is a lover, someone devoted to romantic love.

clue.text: Chap for whom Christmas is put back

indicators.note: put back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: Noel is another name for Christmas

explanation.surface: A man has his festive celebrations postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon is a man's name, and a chap is a man.

clue.text: Merry spills before end of party

parts.note: to tip is to spill or pour

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word party

explanation.surface: A guest gets cheerful and spills drinks before the party ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry is a mild way of saying slightly drunk.

clue.text: Piece of fencing to frustrate?

definitions.meaning: a light sword used in the sport of fencing

explanation.definitionFit: The fencer's blunted sword and the verb to thwart share one spelling.

clue.text: Nelson, for example, in cargo area

definitions.meaning: a nelson is a wrestling grip
the space below deck where freight is stowed

explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a wrestling grip, and a ship stows its freight below deck in the same-named space.

clue.text: Love censorship in Scottish resort

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
a ban is a prohibition, as censorship imposes

explanation.surface: Romance is suppressed in a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a seaside town and ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Tapers like northern shafts

parts.note: arrows are shafts shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Candles resemble shafts of light from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tapers' looks like candles, but it is the verb, gets thinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that narrows becomes thinner towards one end, as a taper does.

clue.text: Italian in Burma, all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters of in Burma are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian travels widely in Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Umbria, a region of central Italy, is Italian.

clue.text: Tendency to follow group lowers talent

parts.note: lowers are animals that low, cattle, which form a herd
an instinct is a natural talent

explanation.surface: Following the crowd puts one's abilities down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' looks like a verb, puts down, but it is things that low, i.e. moo: cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Herd instinct is the urge to think and act as the crowd does.
